references.text: The same chapter forbids uncovering the nakedness of a sister, whether she is your father's daughter or your mother's. Verse 11 elaborates on this by specifying a half-sister born from your father's wife.

It states the punishment for one who takes his sister, either his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and uncovers her nakedness. This is the legal consequence of the violation described in Leviticus 18:11.
A curse is pronounced against anyone who lies with his sister, his father's or his mother's daughter. This confirms the prohibition from Leviticus in the form of a curse.
Ezekiel condemns those in Jerusalem who have violated their sister, their father's daughter. The prophet applies the laws of Leviticus to accuse the people of their sins.
Tamar tells Amnon that he should ask the king for her, suggesting that marriage with a half-sister may have been tolerated in practice, even though Leviticus forbade it.
